account: It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I am at the plaza for my scheduled market walk. So far I have no evidence of an emergency or unusual town business. The secretary said there was no correspondence or urgent news, and Townsfolk 08 and 30 each told me they had no news. Several residents are gathered near the town hall and plaza, but I do not know their purposes. The builder has just appeared nearby carrying a lantern and walking; that may be ordinary work, but I have not asked. This morning the secretary requested my appointment book, which I gave over, then asked again to review it or hear the schedule. I repeated today's appointments and later saw the secretary return the book to its chest. That seems connected to preparing my meetings, as the secretary said, though the repeated request was confusing. I missed a subsequent reply while walking away. The secretary then walked toward the plaza; I do not know where they were going. I still need to establish which east-bank dockside cottage hosts my three o'clock tea. My remaining appointments today are noon lunch at home, one o'clock accounts in the office, three o'clock tea, four-thirty office, and seven o'clock home.
